# QUBO heuristics versus exact and local search methods for cardinality-constrained mean-variance portfolios: a pre-registered anytime benchmark

Code, configurations, registered runs and analyses of the paper by S. M. Avdoshin and K. A. Patrushev (submitted to
*Computers & Operations Research*). Every number, table and figure of the paper is generated by code from the
registered analyses in this repository.

## Contents

- `src/cif/` — the package: the problem, instance families, exact methods (native SCIP model, multi-tree outer
  approximation), the QUBO pipeline and its samplers, local search, anytime metrics, statistics, the experiment
  runner and the analyses.
- `configs/` — the configuration of every stage (`E1`: RQ1, `E2`: RQ2, `E3`: RQ3) and the pilot reports
  (`configs/E2/pilot/`); `configs/E2/README.md` lists the commands of every stage.
- `runs/` — the registered runs: per run `config.json` / `config.yaml`, `manifest.json` (code state, input hashes,
  host, timings), the raw rows `results.jsonl.gz` (one row per cell) and derived tables; `runs/registry.jsonl` lists
  them. The job shards and logs of the server runs are not included.
- `results/E1`, `results/E2`, `results/E3` — the outputs of the analyses that the paper reads.
- `docs/ANALYSIS_PLAN.md` — the pre-registered analysis plan (frozen on 8 October 2026), with the dated deviation
  log in section 12 (in Russian); `docs/prereg/` — the frozen copy and its RFC 3161 timestamp (`.tsq`, `.tsr`).
- `paper/` — the LaTeX sources; `paper/generated/` — numbers, tables and figures written by `scripts/paper_numbers.py`,
  `scripts/paper_tables.py` and `scripts/paper_figures.py`; `paper/refs.bib` is written by `scripts/paper_refs.py`
  from the bibliographies `docs/lit/*.bib`, every entry checked by `tools/lit/verify_bib.py`.
- `tests/` — unit tests (pytest).

## Environment

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml        # Python 3.11; exact versions (linux-64): environment.lock.yml
conda activate cif
pip install -e .
python scripts/unpack_runs.py               # optional: the raw rows of the runs, read by some tests and the analyses
python -m pytest tests -q                   # tests that need the data sets or the unpacked rows skip without them
```

## The paper's numbers, tables and figures

```bash
python scripts/paper_numbers.py --check     # paper/generated/numbers.tex is what the registered analyses give
python scripts/paper_tables.py && python scripts/paper_figures.py
cd paper && latexmk -pdf main.tex
```

## Re-running the analyses and the experiments

```bash
python scripts/unpack_runs.py               # results.jsonl.gz -> results.jsonl in every run directory
```

The analyses are run with `python -m cif.experiments.e1_analysis`, `python -m cif.experiments.e2_analysis` and
`python -m cif.experiments.e3_analysis` on the registered runs; the exact commands and run identifiers are in
`configs/E2/README.md` and in the `inputs` field of every analysis report (`results/**/**.json`).

The experiments need the data sets, which are not redistributed: the 49 industry portfolios and their risk-free rate
(Kenneth French data library; `scripts/data/build_ff49.py`), the US risk-free rate (FRED, series DTB3;
`scripts/data/build_riskfree.py`), the S&P 500 at date (membership from Wikipedia, prices from Yahoo Finance;
`scripts/data/build_sp500_pit_dataset.py`) and the OR-Library problems port1-port5
(<https://people.brunel.ac.uk/~mastjjb/jeb/orlib/portinfo.html>, into `data/raw/orlib/`). The files used have the
hashes recorded in `data/processed/*/provenance.json` (`python -m cif.data.provenance verify ...`). A stage is run with
`python -m cif.experiments.run --config configs/<stream>/<stage>.yaml` (locally) or `scripts/run_server.sh` (at
most 16 single-threaded jobs pinned to physical cores, as in the paper).

## Notes

- The runs were made from the development repository; `manifest.json` records its commit (`git_sha`). This snapshot
  is commit `4c0bc92` of that repository. Its history is not public.
- Some documentation (the analysis plan, comments in configurations) is in Russian.
- The use of an AI coding assistant is described in the paper (Section 4.6 and the declaration).
